pr_title: Always print URL scheme to stdout
pr_comments: Perhaps this is too disruptive, but for terminals that auto-recognize URIs, it helps if the scheme is known. Some might default to assuming "https", but not all - conpty used by wt.exe and cmd.exe apparently doesn't.

issue_context.title: `gh pr create -w` doesn't print absolute URI to stdout
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

When you run `gh pr create -w` it prints a URI without the scheme:

```text
To https://github.com/owner/repo.git
 * [new branch]          HEAD -> branch
branch 'branch' set up to track 'origin/branch'.
Opening github.com/owner/repo/compare/main...branch in your browser.
```

If the browser isn't opened automatically - as is the case by default in WSL without something like wslview installed - you can't `Ctrl+Click` the URI because it doesn't have a scheme.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. In WSL without wslview, or without wslview set the old hack `export BROWSER=explorer.exe`.
2. Run `gh pr create -w`
3. Windows Explorer opens - not the browser - and the URI in the stdout message above isn't clickabke, at least in VSCode's integrated terminal (which is conpty that Windows Terminal uses as well).

### Expected vs actual behavior

Like many (most?) other commands, the scheme should be prefaced before the URI.
comments:
Apparently, this is intentional: <https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/0e690fad0e42abb0e9b0665e9957b0d76eaafd84/internal/text/text.go#L70>

Any reason not to display the scheme? Just display length? Clickable URLs are more common in terminals these days.

Digging up ancient history, there are a few pieces to reassemble this picture:

- https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/1282/files#r456551890
  _highlights some decisions might be related to individual aesthetics_

- https://github.com/cli/cli/commit/90f6a73ba59ed0057e58f56f02201923211cc565
  _not the origin of this but some of the refactor_

- https://github.com/cli/cli/commit/31001877bda166ec433a0d303d443bc174189f97
  _this is the oldest reference I can dig up_

I don't think there is a technical / breaking reason to exclude the protocol in the url.  This will cause various tests to break but those just need to be patched up.

I figured something along the lines of https://github.com/cli/cli/commit/31001877bda166ec433a0d303d443bc174189f97 just to shorten things up. Understandable, but 8 extra characters doesn't seem like much if it makes links clickable; though, I'm was originally thinking of the individual URLs in output messages. However, URLs in runs like `gh pr checks` already had the unmodified URL with the scheme, so maybe this isn't so bad. It's consistent at least.
